Autonomous vehicles are cars and trucks that drive themselves, with sensors and software for perception, prediction, planning and control. The field runs from ALVINN, a 1988 neural network that steered a van from camera and laser range-finder images <Cite id="alvinn-1988" />, to Waymo robotaxis that gave more than 500,000 fully autonomous rides a week in April 2026 <Cite id="alphabet-q1-2026" />.

<Image id="waymo-jaguar-ipace-san-francisco-2023" />

ALVINN trained on simulated road images <Cite id="alvinn-1988" />. By 1991 it learned to drive the Navlab van in under five minutes by watching a human driver <Cite id="pomerleau-1991" />. On the 1995 No Hands Across America tour, CMU's RALPH program steered for 2,797 of 2,849 miles, 98.2 percent, while the researchers handled throttle and brake <Cite id="no-hands-across-america-1995" />. Stanley won the 2005 DARPA Grand Challenge with software built mainly on machine learning and probabilistic reasoning <Cite id="stanley-2006" />.

## The driving stack

A production autonomous vehicle is a pipeline of perception, prediction, planning and control, each with its own models, metrics and failure modes <Cite id="uniad-2023" /><Cite id="paden-2016" />. UniAD calls this "modular tasks in sequential order" <Cite id="uniad-2023" />. Paden's survey adds a vehicle-control layer below motion planning <Cite id="paden-2016" />.

<AvStackTable className="my-6" />

### Perception

Perception turns sensor streams into a model of the scene: which objects exist, where they are, how they move and what the road permits. Waymo's encoder fuses camera, lidar and radar inputs over time <Cite id="waymo-foundation-model-2025" />, and Waymo argues that no single sensor can replicate that redundant view <Cite id="waymo-ai-lessons-2026" />. BEVFormer, a camera-only bird's-eye-view detector, matched lidar-based baselines on the nuScenes test set <Cite id="bevformer-2022" />.

<Image id="waymo-roof-sensor-suite-2025" />

nuScenes, 1,000 scenes of 20 seconds, was the first dataset with a full vehicle sensor suite: 6 cameras, 5 radars and 1 lidar <Cite id="nuscenes-2020" />. The Waymo Open Dataset added 1,150 scenes of synchronized lidar and camera data <Cite id="waymo-open-dataset-2020" />. By its own metric it was 15 times more diverse than the largest earlier camera-plus-lidar set <Cite id="waymo-open-dataset-2020" />. Box detectors struggle with general, out-of-vocabulary objects, so the Occ3D benchmark predicts the occupancy and semantics of the whole scene <Cite id="occ3d-2023" />.

Every later stage inherits a perception error. At Tempe in 2018 the system first detected a pedestrian 5.6 seconds before impact <Cite id="ntsb-uber-2019" />. It classified her in turn as a vehicle, an unknown object and a bicyclist, and never predicted her path correctly <Cite id="ntsb-uber-2019" />.

### Prediction

Prediction estimates what every other agent will do over the next several seconds. The future is multi-modal: a pedestrian may cross or wait, and a predictor that averages the two forecasts a path through neither. The Waymo Open Motion Dataset made interactive forecasting a benchmark: over 100,000 scenes of 20 seconds at 10 Hz, more than 570 hours over 1,750 km of roads <Cite id="waymo-open-motion-2021" />.

Early predictors drew agent histories and map features into a top-down image for a convolutional network. VectorNet replaced that raster with a hierarchical graph network over vectorized polylines <Cite id="vectornet-2020" />. It matched or beat the raster with over 70 percent fewer parameters and an order of magnitude less computation <Cite id="vectornet-2020" />. MotionLM then cast multi-agent forecasting as language modeling over discrete motion tokens <Cite id="motionlm-2023" />.

### Planning

Planning decides the route, lane, speed profile and trajectory for the next few seconds. CMU's Boss won the 2007 DARPA Urban Challenge with a three-layer planner for mission, behavior and motion <Cite id="boss-urban-challenge-2008" />. Paden's survey splits urban planning the same way, with feedback control below <Cite id="paden-2016" />, the families covered under [motion planning](/classical/motion-planning/).

<Image id="cmu-boss-urban-challenge-winner" />

On nuPlan, the first closed-loop machine-learning planning benchmark <Cite id="nuplan-2021" />, an extremely simple planner built on rule-based priors won the 2023 challenge <Cite id="dauner-misconceptions-2023" />. Dauner and colleagues found learned planners limited in complex scenarios <Cite id="dauner-misconceptions-2023" />.

ChauffeurNet, Waymo's 2018 imitative planner, found standard behavior cloning on 30 million examples insufficient, even with perception preparing its inputs and a controller executing its outputs <Cite id="chauffeurnet-2018" />. It perturbed the expert's driving into collisions and off-road excursions and added losses that penalize them <Cite id="chauffeurnet-2018" />. Manipulation later rediscovered that fix for covariate shift, as [behavior cloning foundations](/manipulation/bc-foundations/) explains.

### Control

Control turns a planned trajectory into steering, brake and throttle commands, and holds the vehicle on it despite disturbances, tire nonlinearity and actuator delay. Paden's survey covers the feedback path-tracking families: pure pursuit, Lyapunov-based trajectory tracking and model-predictive control <Cite id="paden-2016" />. A learned planner outputs a trajectory, and a classical [controller](/classical/control/) tracks it.

### Modular versus end-to-end

Each interface between stages is a lossy summary, and an upstream error cannot be corrected downstream. A 2024 survey frames the trade: end-to-end systems optimize perception and planning features jointly, while modular designs are easier to interpret and debug <Cite id="e2e-ad-survey-2024" />. Koopman argues that "safe enough" also requires no risk hot spots, such as reckless driving or risk shifted onto vulnerable populations, plus standards conformance and accountability <Cite id="koopman-safe-enough-2026" />.

<AvSafetyMiles className="my-6" />

US companies must report crashes but not the miles they log, so crash rates are unknown for operators that do not volunteer mileage <Cite id="iihs-waymo-2026" />. NHTSA has also streamlined its Standing General Order on crash reporting <Cite id="nhtsa-av-framework-2026" />. California's DMV says its disengagement reports are not designed for comparison across companies, and deployment-permit operations need not report disengagements at all <Cite id="ca-dmv-av-miles-2026" />.

In September 2026, Chris Paxton argued that an automated system should be judged by its potential for catastrophic failure, which is much higher for a truck: it needs far longer to stop, and when one breaks down on a highway the law requires warning flares that a truck with no one aboard cannot set out <Cite id="paxton-autonomous-trucks-2026" />. He expected driverless trucks to spread over the following year mainly in China and the US Sun Belt, and put highways where ice forms years away <Cite id="paxton-autonomous-trucks-2026" />.

### The deployment record

Waymo's peer-reviewed 2025 study covered 56.7 million rider-only miles through January 2025 <Cite id="waymo-crash-rates-2025" />. Against human benchmarks on the same roads, it found statistically significant lower rates of any-injury-reported, airbag-deployment and suspected-serious-injury crashes <Cite id="waymo-crash-rates-2025" />. Vehicle-to-vehicle intersection crashes with any injury fell 96 percent, with no significant disbenefit in any of its 11 crash-type groups <Cite id="waymo-crash-rates-2025" />.

Waymo's own safety hub reports 271.3 million rider-only miles through June 2026 <Cite id="waymo-safety-hub-2026" />. Over the same distance it counts 95 percent fewer serious-injury-or-worse crashes and 82 percent fewer injury-causing crashes than human drivers <Cite id="waymo-safety-hub-2026" />. IIHS found that Waymo's driverless vehicles in San Francisco, Phoenix, Los Angeles and Austin had 68 percent fewer police-reportable crashes per mile than human drivers <Cite id="iihs-waymo-2026" />.

Tesla says it launched unsupervised rides in Miami, Orlando and Tampa in July 2026 and expanded its unsupervised area in Austin <Cite id="tesla-q2-2026-update" />. Baidu reported in August 2026 that Apollo Go had reached 28 cities and more than 240 million fully driverless kilometres <Cite id="baidu-q2-2026" />. Aurora began driverless customer deliveries between Dallas and Houston in May 2025 after closing its safety case <Cite id="aurora-driverless-launch-2025" />. By its count it drove nearly 440,000 driverless miles through June 2026 with zero collisions attributed to its system, and expected to end the year with 200 driverless trucks <Cite id="aurora-q2-2026" />.

On March 18, 2018, an Uber ATG test vehicle in Tempe, Arizona struck and killed a 49-year-old pedestrian crossing N. Mill Avenue at night, pushing a bicycle, where there was no crosswalk <Cite id="ntsb-uber-2019" />. The system judged a collision imminent 1.2 seconds before impact, and its design precluded emergency braking for crash mitigation alone, relying on the operator <Cite id="ntsb-uber-2019" />. The operator was streaming a television show, glancing down until about one second before the crash <Cite id="ntsb-uber-2019" />. Every layer failed at once, the correlated-safeguard problem the [reliability gap](/frontier/reliability-gap/) article examines.

On October 2, 2023, a driverless Cruise vehicle dragged a pedestrian about 20 feet before stopping. Under a September 2024 consent order, Cruise agreed to a \$1.5 million penalty for crash reports that omitted those details <Cite id="nhtsa-cruise-consent-2024" />. In December 2024 GM stopped funding Cruise's robotaxi work, citing the time and resources needed to scale it <Cite id="gm-cruise-refocus-2024" />.

## The relation to robot learning

The imitation toolkit was built on driving before it reached arms. DAgger, the canonical fix for covariate shift, was demonstrated on steering a car in a 3D racing game <Cite id="dagger-2011" />. It cuts the growth of mistakes over the horizon from quadratic to linear <Cite id="dagger-2011" />. On 500,000 hours of driving, Waymo found that forecasting and planning improve as a power law in compute, and closed-loop metrics improve too <Cite id="waymo-scaling-laws-2025" />.

RAD trains end-to-end policies by reinforcement learning in photorealistic 3D Gaussian splatting replicas, to address imitation's causal confusion and open-loop gap <Cite id="rad-2025" />. It reports a 3x lower collision rate <Cite id="rad-2025" />.

### The convergence is now explicit

EMMA is a vision-language model co-trained as a generalist on planning, detection and road-graph tasks, with its driving outputs written as text <Cite id="emma-2024" />. It is a <Term id="vision-language-action-model">vision-language-action model</Term> whose embodiment is a car. A late-2025 survey splits driving VLAs into end-to-end models, which perceive, reason and plan in one network, and dual-system models, where a slow VLM deliberates over fast, safety-critical execution <Cite id="vla-ad-survey-2026" />.

Waymo's foundation model uses such a "Think Fast and Think Slow" design, a sensor-fusion encoder for rapid reactions beside a driving VLM trained using Gemini <Cite id="waymo-foundation-model-2025" />. The split mirrors the end-to-end versus [hierarchical](/manipulation/hierarchical/) divide in manipulation and the [knowledge insulation](/manipulation/knowledge-insulation/) case for a separate fast path. NVIDIA reports that its Alpamayo-R1 driving VLA runs on the vehicle in real time at 99 ms latency <Cite id="alpamayo-r1-2025" />.

The Waymo Open Dataset set the pattern of shared perception benchmarks <Cite id="waymo-open-dataset-2020" />. Open X-Embodiment pools over a million real robot trajectories across 22 embodiments from 34 labs <Cite id="open-x-embodiment-2023" />. Driving data is counted in hundreds of thousands of hours, such as the 500,000 in Waymo's scaling study <Cite id="waymo-scaling-laws-2025" />, a contrast that [the data bottleneck](/data-hardware/data-bottleneck/) examines.

### What differs in kind

A car steers and accelerates through two channels governed by tire friction and well-studied vehicle models. A manipulator moves dozens of joints that make and break contact. The <Term id="mpc">model-predictive control</Term> that tracks a car's trajectory <Cite id="paden-2016" /> has no equally clean purchase on a robot wiping a table, the argument of [why RL won locomotion](/rl-sim2real/why-rl-locomotion/).

Evaluation differs too. Waymo says replaying recorded data in open-loop simulation is insufficient <Cite id="waymo-ai-lessons-2026" />, and nuPlan moved planning evaluation from open-loop L2 metrics to closed-loop simulation <Cite id="nuplan-2021" />. Manipulation still reports short-horizon success on small trial counts, the subject of the [evaluation crisis](/data-hardware/evaluation-crisis/).

Driving simulation covers rigid-body motion and appearance with no contact-rich phase, and Waymo says its World Model helps it scale its service safely <Cite id="waymo-world-model-2026" />. Robot learning attempts the same with Genie-class models whose range of actions is still constrained <Cite id="genie-3-2025" />.

### What to watch

One open question is whether dual-system driving VLAs settle into the shape of hierarchical manipulation systems <Cite id="vla-ad-survey-2026" />. Another is whether generative simulators extend from appearance into contact. A third is whether robotics adopts AV's safety-case machinery, from formal models like RSS <Cite id="rss-2017" /> to credibility rules for virtual testing <Cite id="un-ads-regulation-2026" />, before robots deploy at scale. [Drones](/adjacent/drones/) covers flight, where a policy trained in simulation has already beaten human champions.

Flight was an early learning success because its dynamics simulate well: a reinforcement-learning system beat human world champions in its own lab in 2023 <Cite id="swift-drone-racing-2023" />, and a one-camera drone won an organiser-run race in 2025 <Cite id="monorace-2026" />.

## Why flight was the first solved testbed

A quadrotor is a benign case for simulation. Its dynamics are differentially flat in position and heading, even with linear rotor drag <Cite id="faessler-flatness-2018" />, and standard models cover its dynamics, estimation and control <Cite id="mahony-multirotor-2012" />. Flight also has no contact: an aerial robot either flies in free space or has already failed. Racing quadrotors still exceed 100 km/h and accelerate at several times gravity <Cite id="swift-drone-racing-2023" />. Make the drone in the figure below climb, fly forward and turn, and watch its four propeller speeds change.

<ExplainerFigure id="flying" />

Classical stacks plan a trajectory and then track it. Mellinger and Kumar generated minimum-snap trajectories for quadrotors <Cite id="mellinger-minimum-snap-2011" />, and Lee and colleagues built a geometric tracking controller on SE(3) <Cite id="lee-se3-control-2010" />. In 2021 time-optimal trajectory planning outperformed professional human pilots in racing <Cite id="foehn-time-optimal-2021" />.

Swift, from the University of Zurich, raced three human champions, including the world champions of two leagues, and won several races against each <Cite id="swift-drone-racing-2023" />. It trained its control policy in simulation with model-free reinforcement learning <Cite id="swift-drone-racing-2023" />. The team then fitted residual models of perception noise and unmodeled dynamics from real flight data and retrained <Cite id="swift-drone-racing-2023" />.

In September 2023, Song and colleagues showed that an RL controller outperformed optimal control on the same racing task <Cite id="racing-rl-vs-oc-2023" />. Optimal control splits the problem into planning and control with a trajectory as the interface, which limits the controller under unmodeled effects. RL optimizes a task-level objective directly and handles model uncertainty through domain randomization; it flew above 12 g and 108 km/h <Cite id="racing-rl-vs-oc-2023" />. A later hybrid embedded a differentiable MPC in an actor-critic framework and matched model-free RL at up to 21 m/s <Cite id="ac-mpc-2026" />.

In April 2025 a TU Delft drone with one rolling-shutter camera and an IMU won the A2RL race in Abu Dhabi, beating all AI teams and three human world champions in a knockout tournament <Cite id="monorace-2026" />. TU Delft notes that Swift raced in a lab where the researchers controlled conditions, hardware and track, while the A2RL organisers designed both hardware and track <Cite id="tudelft-a2rl-2025" />.

In January 2026 world FPV champion Minchan Kim beat TII Racing's drone from a 4 to 4 tie when it struck a gate and could not recover <Cite id="a2rl-2026-final" />. Champion policies stay narrow: they often crash immediately in unseen configurations, and a 2026 method improved generalization 7.4x <Cite id="green-generalization-2026" />.

<DroneChampionsTimeline className="my-6" />

## The autonomy stack on a flying robot

One camera and one low-cost IMU are the minimum sensor suite for metric six-DoF state estimation <Cite id="vins-mono-2018" />. <Term id="visual-inertial-odometry">Visual-inertial odometry</Term> fuses image features with IMU measurements into the pose and velocity the controller needs, without GPS or motion capture <Cite id="swift-drone-racing-2023" />. The fast inner loop often runs on a microcontroller stack such as PX4, which has substantially lower latency than a typical robotics Linux system <Cite id="px4-2015" />.

<Image id="dji-mavic-pro-in-flight" />

### Perception latency bounds the whole system

Falanga, Kim and Scaramuzza asked how fast a drone can fly given its perception latency and the acceleration its airframe can produce <Cite id="falanga-latency-2019" />. A drone at speed $v$ sees an obstacle at sensing range $s$, and its pipeline delays that information by latency $\tau$. Avoiding the obstacle at maximum lateral acceleration $u$ takes time proportional to the square root of obstacle size over $u$. If $s/v - \tau$ is shorter than the maneuver, no controller saves the drone <Cite id="falanga-latency-2019" />.

A 70 ms stereo pipeline, the upper bound the study took from a commercial camera's datasheet, supports about 19 m/s at 25 m/s² of lateral acceleration and 25 m/s at 50 m/s² <Cite id="falanga-latency-2019" />. An event camera reports per-pixel brightness changes without waiting for a frame. At 8 m of range its ceiling is 7 percent higher on the least agile airframe and 22 percent higher at 50 m/s², 31.03 against 25.40 m/s. The paper's own summary of 7 to 12 percent is for its most agile airframe, at 200 m/s², against the fastest stereo camera <Cite id="falanga-latency-2019" />.

In 2020 an event-camera quadrotor dodged fast-moving objects using only onboard sensing and computation <Cite id="falanga-event-avoidance-2020" />. Vision-language-action flight is far slower: RaceVLA averaged 1.04 m/s with a top speed of 2.02 m/s <Cite id="racevla-2025" />. On the CognitiveDrone benchmark RaceVLA succeeded 31.3 percent of the time, and CognitiveDrone-R1, which adds a reasoning module, 77.2 percent <Cite id="cognitivedrone-2025" />.

Jaewoo Lee, Guanya Shi and colleagues at Seoul National University, Carnegie Mellon and elsewhere (October 2026) let a coding agent that programs an aerial manipulator run diagnostic programs in simulation, such as a camera move or a test lift, before it declares a task done <Cite id="fly-by-code-2026" />. Over six simulated tasks and 60 trials per condition, the authors report 75 percent success against 31.7 percent with execution logs and final images <Cite id="fly-by-code-2026" />. Unmodified, the programs completed 4 of 5 real two-object pick-and-place trials and 3 of 5 cabinet trials <Cite id="fly-by-code-2026" />.

### End-to-end learning skips the interfaces

Deep Drone Acrobatics trained a policy entirely in simulation by imitating an optimal controller with privileged information, and flew maneuvers at up to 3 g <Cite id="deep-drone-acrobatics-2020" />. In 2021 Loquercio and colleagues used the same recipe to map noisy depth images directly to collision-free trajectories <Cite id="high-speed-flight-2021" />. With realistic simulated sensor noise, the policy transferred to forests, snow, derailed trains and collapsed buildings with no additional training. The authors argue that separating sensing, mapping and planning "can be problematic for high-speed navigation in cluttered environments" because latency compounds and errors propagate <Cite id="high-speed-flight-2021" />.

Swift kept a modular front end: a visual-inertial estimator and a gate-detection network feed a Kalman filter, and a small two-layer RL network maps that state to collective thrust and body rates <Cite id="swift-drone-racing-2023" />. Later systems drop explicit state estimation. Geles and colleagues fly from pixels with the thrust and body-rate commands human pilots use <Cite id="geles-pixels-2024" />, and Dream to Fly learned racing from pixels with a world model where PPO and SAC struggled <Cite id="dream-to-fly-2025" />.

MonoRace keeps a state estimator, but its network skips inner-loop controllers and sends motor commands at 500 Hz <Cite id="monorace-2026" />. Training through differentiable physics produced a depth-to-control policy that flies forests at up to 20 m/s on a \$21 computer <Cite id="zhang-diff-physics-2025" />.

## Swarm robotics

Swarm robotics uses many cheap platforms to cover a search area, map a forest or fly a light show. Its founding models came from biology, Reynolds' 1987 flocking model being the canonical one <Cite id="reynolds-boids-1987" />, and treat the group as a dynamical system of local attraction and repulsion. Vásárhelyi and colleagues optimized those terms and flew 30 drones in coherent outdoor flocking <Cite id="vasarhelyi-flocking-2018" />. Reactive models have no lookahead.

<SwarmControlTable className="my-6" />

Soria, Schiano and Floreano folded the interaction terms into a nonlinear model-predictive controller with obstacle and neighbour terms <Cite id="soria-nmpc-swarm-2021" />. In simulation it flew faster and with fewer collisions than the reactive equivalent, and five quadrotors flew it through a real indoor obstacle field <Cite id="soria-nmpc-swarm-2021" />. EGO-Swarm's agents generate safe, dynamically feasible trajectories in several milliseconds over an unreliable trajectory-sharing network <Cite id="ego-swarm-2021" />.

Zhou and colleagues ran a spatial-temporal trajectory optimizer on palm-sized drones, solving in milliseconds from onboard sensing with no external localization <Cite id="micro-drone-swarm-2022" />. Ten of them flew through a dense bamboo forest <Cite id="micro-drone-swarm-2022" />. The differentiable-physics policy coordinates several drones without communication or centralized planning <Cite id="zhang-diff-physics-2025" />. Multi-agent RL with league self-play beat a champion-level human pilot in multi-player races above 22 m/s and cut collisions by 50 percent against single-agent baselines <Cite id="geles-marl-2026" />.

Everything cited above coordinates implicitly; none of it decides who goes where. In Ukraine, electronic warfare is pushing military drones toward terrain-based navigation, autonomous target lock-on and, eventually, mesh-networked swarms <Cite id="spectrum-ukraine-autonomy-2026" />.

## Delivery and regulation

Zipline reports more than 3 million deliveries and more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles since its first commercial delivery in 2016 <Cite id="zipline-safety-facts" />. In January 2026 it reported US delivery growth of about 15 percent week over week for seven months <Cite id="zipline-2m-2026" />. Wing reports well over one million commercial deliveries and plans more than 270 Walmart locations reaching 40 million Americans by 2027 <Cite id="wing-walmart-2026" />. Walmart reported 1 million drone deliveries in May 2026, from 66 stores in four states <Cite id="walmart-drone-1m-2026" />.

<DroneDeliveryCounts className="my-6" />

The FAA and TSA proposed Part 108 in August 2025 to enable routine flight beyond visual line of sight <Cite id="faa-part-108-nprm-2025" />. The FAA reopened comments on electronic conspicuity and right-of-way until February 11, 2026 <Cite id="faa-part-108-reopen-2026" />.

## What the rest of robotics takes from it

Latency budgets transfer directly. A policy that infers at 20 Hz controls a contact-rich task at about 20 Hz whatever the arm's bandwidth, the reasoning the perception-latency study formalised for flight <Cite id="falanga-latency-2019" />. [Real-time execution](/manipulation/realtime-execution/) covers that budget for manipulators.

The sim-to-real recipe also carries over: residual models fitted from real data <Cite id="swift-drone-racing-2023" /> plus privileged imitation with realistic sensor noise <Cite id="high-speed-flight-2021" />. [Sim-to-real transfer](/rl-sim2real/sim2real-transfer/) and [parallel simulation](/rl-sim2real/parallel-sim-rl/) cover it for other robots.

Champion claims need context. Swift won in its own lab and MonoRace on organiser hardware <Cite id="tudelft-a2rl-2025" />, and the 2026 final turned on one unrecovered gate strike <Cite id="a2rl-2026-final" />. The distance between peak and reliable performance is the [reliability gap](/frontier/reliability-gap/), and [surgical robotics](/adjacent/surgical/) shows a bar cleared under regulatory oversight.

In September 2023, Song and colleagues showed that an RL controller outperformed optimal control on the same racing task <Cite id="racing-rl-vs-oc-2023" />. Optimal control splits the problem into planning and control with a trajectory as the interface, which limits the controller under unmodeled effects. RL optimizes a task-level objective directly and handles model uncertainty through domain randomization; it flew above 12 g and 108 km/h <Cite id="racing-rl-vs-oc-2023" />. A later hybrid embedded a differentiable MPC in an actor-critic framework and matched model-free RL at up to 21 m/s <Cite id="ac-mpc-2026" />.

In April 2025 a TU Delft drone with one rolling-shutter camera and an IMU won the A2RL race in Abu Dhabi, beating all AI teams and three human world champions in a knockout tournament <Cite id="monorace-2026" />. TU Delft notes that Swift raced in a lab where the researchers controlled conditions, hardware and track, while the A2RL organisers designed both hardware and track <Cite id="tudelft-a2rl-2025" />.

In January 2026 world FPV champion Minchan Kim beat TII Racing's drone from a 4 to 4 tie when it struck a gate and could not recover <Cite id="a2rl-2026-final" />. Champion policies stay narrow: they often crash immediately in unseen configurations, and a 2026 method improved generalization 7.4x <Cite id="green-generalization-2026" />.

<DroneChampionsTimeline className="my-6" />

## The autonomy stack on a flying robot

One camera and one low-cost IMU are the minimum sensor suite for metric six-DoF state estimation <Cite id="vins-mono-2018" />. <Term id="visual-inertial-odometry">Visual-inertial odometry</Term> fuses image features with IMU measurements into the pose and velocity the controller needs, without GPS or motion capture <Cite id="swift-drone-racing-2023" />. The fast inner loop often runs on a microcontroller stack such as PX4, which has substantially lower latency than a typical robotics Linux system <Cite id="px4-2015" />.

<Image id="dji-mavic-pro-in-flight" />

### Perception latency bounds the whole system

Falanga, Kim and Scaramuzza asked how fast a drone can fly given its perception latency and the acceleration its airframe can produce <Cite id="falanga-latency-2019" />. A drone at speed $v$ sees an obstacle at sensing range $s$, and its pipeline delays that information by latency $\tau$. Avoiding the obstacle at maximum lateral acceleration $u$ takes time proportional to the square root of obstacle size over $u$. If $s/v - \tau$ is shorter than the maneuver, no controller saves the drone <Cite id="falanga-latency-2019" />.

A 70 ms stereo pipeline, the upper bound the study took from a commercial camera's datasheet, supports about 19 m/s at 25 m/s² of lateral acceleration and 25 m/s at 50 m/s² <Cite id="falanga-latency-2019" />. An event camera reports per-pixel brightness changes without waiting for a frame. At 8 m of range its ceiling is 7 percent higher on the least agile airframe and 22 percent higher at 50 m/s², 31.03 against 25.40 m/s. The paper's own summary of 7 to 12 percent is for its most agile airframe, at 200 m/s², against the fastest stereo camera <Cite id="falanga-latency-2019" />.

Motion can also preserve the information the camera needs. PAMPC optimizes a point's visibility and motion in the image while respecting the quadrotor's dynamics and input limits <Cite id="pampc-2018" />.

In 2020 an event-camera quadrotor dodged fast-moving objects using only onboard sensing and computation <Cite id="falanga-event-avoidance-2020" />. Vision-language-action flight is far slower: RaceVLA averaged 1.04 m/s with a top speed of 2.02 m/s <Cite id="racevla-2025" />. On the CognitiveDrone benchmark RaceVLA succeeded 31.3 percent of the time, and CognitiveDrone-R1, which adds a reasoning module, 77.2 percent <Cite id="cognitivedrone-2025" />.

Jaewoo Lee, Guanya Shi and colleagues at Seoul National University, Carnegie Mellon and elsewhere (October 2026) let a coding agent that programs an aerial manipulator run diagnostic programs in simulation, such as a camera move or a test lift, before it declares a task done <Cite id="fly-by-code-2026" />. Over six simulated tasks and 60 trials per condition, the authors report 75 percent success against 31.7 percent with execution logs and final images <Cite id="fly-by-code-2026" />. Unmodified, the programs completed 4 of 5 real two-object pick-and-place trials and 3 of 5 cabinet trials <Cite id="fly-by-code-2026" />.

### End-to-end learning skips the interfaces

Real failures can supply supervision too. Learning to Fly by Crashing collected 11,500 crashes and combined the failed approaches with successful portions of the same trajectories to train a navigation policy <Cite id="learning-crash-2017" />.

Deep Drone Acrobatics trained a policy entirely in simulation by imitating an optimal controller with privileged information, and flew maneuvers at up to 3 g <Cite id="deep-drone-acrobatics-2020" />. In 2021 Loquercio and colleagues used the same recipe to map noisy depth images directly to collision-free trajectories <Cite id="high-speed-flight-2021" />. With realistic simulated sensor noise, the policy transferred to forests, snow, derailed trains and collapsed buildings with no additional training. The authors argue that separating sensing, mapping and planning "can be problematic for high-speed navigation in cluttered environments" because latency compounds and errors propagate <Cite id="high-speed-flight-2021" />.

Swift kept a modular front end: a visual-inertial estimator and a gate-detection network feed a Kalman filter, and a small two-layer RL network maps that state to collective thrust and body rates <Cite id="swift-drone-racing-2023" />. Later systems drop explicit state estimation. Geles and colleagues fly from pixels with the thrust and body-rate commands human pilots use <Cite id="geles-pixels-2024" />, and Dream to Fly learned racing from pixels with a world model where PPO and SAC struggled <Cite id="dream-to-fly-2025" />.

MonoRace keeps a state estimator, but its network skips inner-loop controllers and sends motor commands at 500 Hz <Cite id="monorace-2026" />. Training through differentiable physics produced a depth-to-control policy that flies forests at up to 20 m/s on a \$21 computer <Cite id="zhang-diff-physics-2025" />.

## Swarm robotics

Swarm robotics uses many cheap platforms to cover a search area, map a forest or fly a light show. Its founding models came from biology, Reynolds' 1987 flocking model being the canonical one <Cite id="reynolds-boids-1987" />, and treat the group as a dynamical system of local attraction and repulsion. Vásárhelyi and colleagues optimized those terms and flew 30 drones in coherent outdoor flocking <Cite id="vasarhelyi-flocking-2018" />. Reactive models have no lookahead.

<SwarmControlTable className="my-6" />

Soria, Schiano and Floreano folded the interaction terms into a nonlinear model-predictive controller with obstacle and neighbour terms <Cite id="soria-nmpc-swarm-2021" />. In simulation it flew faster and with fewer collisions than the reactive equivalent, and five quadrotors flew it through a real indoor obstacle field <Cite id="soria-nmpc-swarm-2021" />. EGO-Swarm's agents generate safe, dynamically feasible trajectories in several milliseconds over an unreliable trajectory-sharing network <Cite id="ego-swarm-2021" />.

Zhou and colleagues ran a spatial-temporal trajectory optimizer on palm-sized drones, solving in milliseconds from onboard sensing with no external localization <Cite id="micro-drone-swarm-2022" />. Ten of them flew through a dense bamboo forest <Cite id="micro-drone-swarm-2022" />. The differentiable-physics policy coordinates several drones without communication or centralized planning <Cite id="zhang-diff-physics-2025" />. Multi-agent RL with league self-play beat a champion-level human pilot in multi-player races above 22 m/s and cut collisions by 50 percent against single-agent baselines <Cite id="geles-marl-2026" />.

Everything cited above coordinates implicitly; none of it decides who goes where. In Ukraine, electronic warfare is pushing military drones toward terrain-based navigation, autonomous target lock-on and, eventually, mesh-networked swarms <Cite id="spectrum-ukraine-autonomy-2026" />.

## Delivery and regulation

Zipline reports more than 3 million deliveries and more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles since its first commercial delivery in 2016 <Cite id="zipline-safety-facts" />. In January 2026 it reported US delivery growth of about 15 percent week over week for seven months <Cite id="zipline-2m-2026" />. Wing reports well over one million commercial deliveries and plans more than 270 Walmart locations reaching 40 million Americans by 2027 <Cite id="wing-walmart-2026" />. Walmart reported 1 million drone deliveries in May 2026, from 66 stores in four states <Cite id="walmart-drone-1m-2026" />.

<DroneDeliveryCounts className="my-6" />

The FAA and TSA proposed Part 108 in August 2025 to enable routine flight beyond visual line of sight <Cite id="faa-part-108-nprm-2025" />. The FAA reopened comments on electronic conspicuity and right-of-way until February 11, 2026 <Cite id="faa-part-108-reopen-2026" />.

## What the rest of robotics takes from it

Latency budgets transfer directly. A policy that infers at 20 Hz controls a contact-rich task at about 20 Hz whatever the arm's bandwidth, the reasoning the perception-latency study formalised for flight <Cite id="falanga-latency-2019" />. [Real-time execution](/manipulation/realtime-execution/) covers that budget for manipulators.

The sim-to-real recipe also carries over: residual models fitted from real data <Cite id="swift-drone-racing-2023" /> plus privileged imitation with realistic sensor noise <Cite id="high-speed-flight-2021" />. [Sim-to-real transfer](/rl-sim2real/sim2real-transfer/) and [parallel simulation](/rl-sim2real/parallel-sim-rl/) cover it for other robots.

Champion claims need context. Swift won in its own lab and MonoRace on organiser hardware <Cite id="tudelft-a2rl-2025" />, and the 2026 final turned on one unrecovered gate strike <Cite id="a2rl-2026-final" />. The distance between peak and reliable performance is the [reliability gap](/frontier/reliability-gap/), and [surgical robotics](/adjacent/surgical/) shows a bar cleared under regulatory oversight.

Surgical robotics is the use of robots to position or move surgical instruments, today mostly teleoperated systems for <Term id="minimally-invasive-surgery">minimally invasive surgery</Term> that scale and filter a surgeon's hand motion. Intuitive had 11,710 da Vinci systems installed by June 30, 2026 <Cite id="intuitive-q2-2026" />, and most commercial platforms sit at level 0, with no decision autonomy <Cite id="attanasio-autonomy-2021" />.

<Image id="da-vinci-xi-patient-cart-2018" />

## The teleoperation baseline

A da Vinci surgeon sits at a console away from the table and moves hand controllers, while patient-side arms carry wristed instruments and an endoscope. The robot adds motion scaling, tremor filtering and wrists that articulate inside the body. Yang and colleagues place such a system at Level 0, no autonomy, because even with motion scaling its output represents the surgeon's desired motion <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />. At level 1 a robot gives cognitive and physical assistance, and at level 2 it performs a surgical task autonomously <Cite id="attanasio-autonomy-2021" />.

<Image id="da-vinci-xi-surgeon-console-vesoul-2023" />

<MotionPantograph className="my-6" />

The field began with positioning. In 1988 Kwoh and colleagues reported a robot with improved absolute positioning accuracy for CT-guided stereotactic brain surgery <Cite id="kwoh-ct-robot-1988" />. Marescaux and colleagues reported transatlantic robot-assisted telesurgery in 2001 <Cite id="marescaux-telesurgery-2001" />. Intuitive says cardiac surgery was the first specialty cleared on the original da Vinci, in 2002 <Cite id="davinci5-cardiac-2026" />.

Da Vinci 5, cleared in March 2024, has more than 150 enhancements over Xi and more than 10,000 times its computing power <Cite id="davinci5-clearance-2024" />. Its optional Force Feedback instruments let the surgeon feel forces at the instrument tips, and Intuitive reported up to 43 percent less force on tissue in preclinical trials <Cite id="davinci5-clearance-2024" />. In a preclinical study by 28 surgeons, the feature at its high setting cut maximal force by 36, 41 and 55 percent in retraction, dissection and suturing <Cite id="awad-force-feedback-2024" />.

Logs from 444 thoracic procedures by 73 surgeons show median tip force falling from 1.79 N with feedback off to 1.32 N at the high setting <Cite id="kneuertz-dv5-force-2025" />. A pilot study of 68 colorectal operations found less applied force without a significant change in bowel function or length of stay <Cite id="chang-dv5-colorectal-2025" />. In January 2026 the FDA cleared da Vinci 5 for selected cardiac procedures using instruments without force feedback <Cite id="davinci5-cardiac-2026" />.

Intuitive reports that its installed base grew 12 percent in 2025 to 11,106 systems, and that da Vinci procedures grew roughly 18 percent worldwide in 2025 <Cite id="intuitive-q4-2025" />. Of 532 fourth-quarter placements, 303 were da Vinci 5s <Cite id="intuitive-q4-2025" />. In the second quarter of 2026, procedures grew about 15 percent and 246 of 468 placements were da Vinci 5s <Cite id="intuitive-q2-2026" />.

<SurgicalSystemsTable className="my-6 wide-measure" />

Every system in the table is Level 0 or Level 1 on the Yang scale <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />.

## The challengers and what they compete on

CMR Surgical's Versius is a modular multiport system whose arms are separate bedside units that can move between operating rooms, driven from an open console <Cite id="cmr-versius-authorization-2024" />. In October 2024 the FDA authorized it through De Novo for adult cholecystectomy, the first multiport soft-tissue general surgical system authorized that way <Cite id="cmr-versius-authorization-2024" />. CMR put robot-assisted surgery at about 2.5 percent of nearly 10 million annual US major operating-room procedures <Cite id="cmr-versius-authorization-2024" />. Versius Plus was cleared in December 2025, and by March 2026 CMR reported more than 45,000 Versius patients in more than 30 countries <Cite id="versius-plus-510k-2025" /><Cite id="cmr-45000-patients-2026" />.

Medtronic's Hugo was cleared on December 3, 2025 for urologic procedures including prostatectomy, nephrectomy and cystectomy <Cite id="medtronic-hugo-clearance-2025" />. Medtronic says it had already been used in more than 30 countries <Cite id="medtronic-hugo-clearance-2025" />. Its first US case followed at Cleveland Clinic in February 2026 <Cite id="medtronic-hugo-first-us-2026" />.

Medtronic says about 80 percent of US abdominal urologic surgery is already robot-assisted <Cite id="medtronic-hugo-first-us-2026" />. In June 2026 it filed 510(k)s for general and gynecologic surgery <Cite id="medtronic-hugo-510k-2026" />.

Johnson & Johnson's OTTAVA, a table-integrated soft-tissue robot, received De Novo authorization in July 2026 for general-surgery procedures including gastric bypass, cholecystectomy and hiatal hernia repair <Cite id="jnj-ottava-2026" />. J&J says it occupies 30 to 50 percent less space than boom- and cart-mounted systems <Cite id="jnj-ottava-2026" />. In a Michigan registry of 169,404 patients, robotic use in common general-surgery procedures rose from 1.8 percent in 2012 to 15.1 percent in 2018 <Cite id="sheetz-adoption-2020" />.

Moon Surgical's Maestro is a two-armed assistant that holds and positions the laparoscopic camera and instruments, using the cameras and graspers a hospital already owns. Its first 510(k), in December 2022, rested on substantial equivalence to a 1990s endoscope positioner <Cite id="maestro-tavac-2023" />. A single surgeon used it without an assistant in a 30-patient series <Cite id="maestro-tavac-2023" />.

The commercial system was cleared in June 2024 <Cite id="maestro-commercial-510k-2024" />. ScoPilot, cleared in March 2025, runs on NVIDIA Holoscan on the robot and lets the laparoscope follow the instrument tip on demand <Cite id="scopilot-clearance-2025" />, Level 1 assistance on the Yang scale <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />.

<ScopeFollow className="my-6" />

## The precision and reliability bar

A policy that succeeds 95 percent of the time per step compounds to 21.5 percent over 30 steps, the arithmetic of the [reliability gap](/frontier/reliability-gap/). FDA reports on robotic surgery from 2000 to 2013 included 144 deaths (1.4 percent of 10,624 reports), 1,391 patient injuries and 8,061 device malfunctions <Cite id="alemzadeh-adverse-events-2016" />. At clearance, Intuitive said da Vinci 5 would first go to a small number of US customers to gather data on real use <Cite id="davinci5-clearance-2024" />. In the ROLARR trial of 471 rectal-cancer patients, robotic assistance did not significantly reduce conversion to open surgery: 8.1 percent against 12.2 percent for conventional laparoscopy (P = .16) <Cite id="rolarr-2017" />.

In 2016 STAR, the Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot, performed supervised autonomous soft-tissue anastomosis in vivo in pigs <Cite id="star-suturing-2016" />. Its suture spacing and leak pressure matched or exceeded both expert surgeons and robot-assisted technique <Cite id="star-suturing-2016" />. In 2022 a robot performed laparoscopic small-bowel anastomosis in pigs over a one-week survival period, with the operator choosing among autonomously generated plans <Cite id="saeidi-laparoscopic-2022" />. It outperformed expert manual and robot-assisted technique on consistency and accuracy <Cite id="saeidi-laparoscopic-2022" />.

In 2025 SRT-H, whose high-level language policy guides a low-level policy through long-horizon steps and helps it recover from errors, ran ex vivo cholecystectomy experiments <Cite id="srt-h-2025" />. It succeeded on all eight gallbladders tested without human intervention <Cite id="srt-h-2025" />. [Hierarchical policies](/manipulation/hierarchical/) covers that design.

<SurgicalAutonomyLadder className="my-6" />

A device is authorized for an indication, a named procedure in a named population, and expansion needs a new clearance. Yang and colleagues argue that a highly autonomous robot starts practicing medicine, which in the US falls to medical societies <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />. They propose licensing robotic surgeons through the medical establishment, as is done for human surgeons <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />.

Yang and colleagues put the gap between the 510(k) and premarket-approval pathways at tens of millions of dollars and years of review, and add that risk tolerance to autonomous robots is expected to change as autonomous machines such as self-driving cars become commonplace <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />. Haidegger names the lack of autonomy benchmarks and standards as a major barrier to commercialising autonomous surgical robots <Cite id="haidegger-autonomy-2019" />, and [safety and assurance](/frontier/safety-and-assurance/) covers the general case.

## What robot learning takes from it

Clinical recordings could become training data. SRT showed that imitation learning works on the da Vinci despite its approximate kinematics, using a relative action formulation, so the large repository of clinical data may be used for robot learning without further corrections <Cite id="srt-2024" />. Open-H-Embodiment pools synchronized video and kinematics from more than 50 institutions and platforms including Versius, da Vinci, the da Vinci Research Kit and Maestro <Cite id="open-h-embodiment-2026" />.

Its GR00T-H model was the only one evaluated to finish a structured suturing benchmark end to end, in 25 percent of trials against 0 percent for all others <Cite id="open-h-embodiment-2026" />. It reached a 64 percent average <Term id="success-rate">success rate</Term> across a 29-step ex vivo suturing sequence <Cite id="open-h-embodiment-2026" />. [Major datasets](/data-hardware/datasets/) lists its general-robotics peers.

In September 2026, Shutong Jin, Ken Goldberg and colleagues reported AGRO-SUVIDE, a coding-agent framework that builds debridement skills from one expert demonstration and retries a skill when its checks fail. In 340 physical trials on the da Vinci Research Kit, it removed single fragments from a viscoelastic substrate with 85% average success and completed three consecutive removals 60% of the time, or 95% with one human intervention <Cite id="agro-suvide-2026" />.

Intuitive says da Vinci 5's <Term id="force-feedback">Force Feedback</Term> measurements add a new data stream to surgical data science <Cite id="davinci5-clearance-2024" />, and Moon Surgical frames Maestro's sensing and onboard compute as the substrate for next-generation physical AI <Cite id="scopilot-clearance-2025" />. A 2022 review found surgical data science still lacking translational success stories, and its roadmap covers data acquisition under regulatory constraints, annotation and sharing <Cite id="maier-hein-sds-2022" />. The same question of how much evidence earns autonomy runs through [autonomous vehicles](/adjacent/autonomous-vehicles/), [drones](/adjacent/drones/) and [space robotics](/adjacent/space/).

Every system in the table is Level 0 or Level 1 on the Yang scale <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />.

## The challengers and what they compete on

CMR Surgical's Versius is a modular multiport system whose arms are separate bedside units that can move between operating rooms, driven from an open console <Cite id="cmr-versius-authorization-2024" />. In October 2024 the FDA authorized it through De Novo for adult cholecystectomy, the first multiport soft-tissue general surgical system authorized that way <Cite id="cmr-versius-authorization-2024" />. CMR put robot-assisted surgery at about 2.5 percent of nearly 10 million annual US major operating-room procedures <Cite id="cmr-versius-authorization-2024" />. Versius Plus was cleared in December 2025, and by March 2026 CMR reported more than 45,000 Versius patients in more than 30 countries <Cite id="versius-plus-510k-2025" /><Cite id="cmr-45000-patients-2026" />.

Medtronic's Hugo was cleared on December 3, 2025 for urologic procedures including prostatectomy, nephrectomy and cystectomy <Cite id="medtronic-hugo-clearance-2025" />. Medtronic says it had already been used in more than 30 countries <Cite id="medtronic-hugo-clearance-2025" />. Its first US case followed at Cleveland Clinic in February 2026 <Cite id="medtronic-hugo-first-us-2026" />.

Medtronic says about 80 percent of US abdominal urologic surgery is already robot-assisted <Cite id="medtronic-hugo-first-us-2026" />. In June 2026 it filed 510(k)s for general and gynecologic surgery <Cite id="medtronic-hugo-510k-2026" />.

Johnson & Johnson's OTTAVA, a table-integrated soft-tissue robot, received De Novo authorization in July 2026 for general-surgery procedures including gastric bypass, cholecystectomy and hiatal hernia repair <Cite id="jnj-ottava-2026" />. J&J says it occupies 30 to 50 percent less space than boom- and cart-mounted systems <Cite id="jnj-ottava-2026" />. In a Michigan registry of 169,404 patients, robotic use in common general-surgery procedures rose from 1.8 percent in 2012 to 15.1 percent in 2018 <Cite id="sheetz-adoption-2020" />.

Moon Surgical's Maestro is a two-armed assistant that holds and positions the laparoscopic camera and instruments, using the cameras and graspers a hospital already owns. Its first 510(k), in December 2022, rested on substantial equivalence to a 1990s endoscope positioner <Cite id="maestro-tavac-2023" />. A single surgeon used it without an assistant in a 30-patient series <Cite id="maestro-tavac-2023" />.

The commercial system was cleared in June 2024 <Cite id="maestro-commercial-510k-2024" />. ScoPilot, cleared in March 2025, runs on NVIDIA Holoscan on the robot and lets the laparoscope follow the instrument tip on demand <Cite id="scopilot-clearance-2025" />, Level 1 assistance on the Yang scale <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />.

<ScopeFollow className="my-6" />

## The precision and reliability bar

A policy that succeeds 95 percent of the time per step compounds to 21.5 percent over 30 steps, the arithmetic of the [reliability gap](/frontier/reliability-gap/). FDA reports on robotic surgery from 2000 to 2013 included 144 deaths (1.4 percent of 10,624 reports), 1,391 patient injuries and 8,061 device malfunctions <Cite id="alemzadeh-adverse-events-2016" />. At clearance, Intuitive said da Vinci 5 would first go to a small number of US customers to gather data on real use <Cite id="davinci5-clearance-2024" />. In the ROLARR trial of 471 rectal-cancer patients, robotic assistance did not significantly reduce conversion to open surgery: 8.1 percent against 12.2 percent for conventional laparoscopy (P = .16) <Cite id="rolarr-2017" />.

In 2016 STAR, the Smart Tissue Autonomous Robot, performed supervised autonomous soft-tissue anastomosis in vivo in pigs <Cite id="star-suturing-2016" />. Its suture spacing and leak pressure matched or exceeded both expert surgeons and robot-assisted technique <Cite id="star-suturing-2016" />. In 2022 a robot performed laparoscopic small-bowel anastomosis in pigs over a one-week survival period, with the operator choosing among autonomously generated plans <Cite id="saeidi-laparoscopic-2022" />. It outperformed expert manual and robot-assisted technique on consistency and accuracy <Cite id="saeidi-laparoscopic-2022" />.

In 2025 SRT-H, whose high-level language policy guides a low-level policy through long-horizon steps and helps it recover from errors, ran ex vivo cholecystectomy experiments <Cite id="srt-h-2025" />. It succeeded on all eight gallbladders tested without human intervention <Cite id="srt-h-2025" />. [Hierarchical policies](/manipulation/hierarchical/) covers that design.

<SurgicalAutonomyLadder className="my-6" />

A device is authorized for an indication, a named procedure in a named population, and expansion needs a new clearance. Yang and colleagues argue that a highly autonomous robot starts practicing medicine, which in the US falls to medical societies <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />. They propose licensing robotic surgeons through the medical establishment, as is done for human surgeons <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />.

Yang and colleagues put the gap between the 510(k) and premarket-approval pathways at tens of millions of dollars and years of review, and add that risk tolerance to autonomous robots is expected to change as autonomous machines such as self-driving cars become commonplace <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />. Haidegger names the lack of autonomy benchmarks and standards as a major barrier to commercialising autonomous surgical robots <Cite id="haidegger-autonomy-2019" />, and [safety and assurance](/frontier/safety-and-assurance/) covers the general case.

## What robot learning takes from it

The da Vinci Research Kit exposes all control layers through open electronics and software built around retired first-generation da Vinci mechanics <Cite id="dvrk-research-kit-2014" />.

Clinical recordings could become training data. SRT showed that imitation learning works on the da Vinci despite its approximate kinematics, using a relative action formulation, so the large repository of clinical data may be used for robot learning without further corrections <Cite id="srt-2024" />. Open-H-Embodiment pools synchronized video and kinematics from more than 50 institutions and platforms including Versius, da Vinci, the da Vinci Research Kit and Maestro <Cite id="open-h-embodiment-2026" />.

Its GR00T-H model was the only one evaluated to finish a structured suturing benchmark end to end, in 25 percent of trials against 0 percent for all others <Cite id="open-h-embodiment-2026" />. It reached a 64 percent average <Term id="success-rate">success rate</Term> across a 29-step ex vivo suturing sequence <Cite id="open-h-embodiment-2026" />. [Major datasets](/data-hardware/datasets/) lists its general-robotics peers.

The data labels serve different purposes. JIGSAWS synchronizes video and robot kinematics with surgical-gesture annotations <Cite id="jigsaws-benchmark-2017" />. EndoNet jointly learns operation-phase recognition and tool-presence detection from laparoscopic video <Cite id="endonet-2016" />. CholecT50 describes actions as instrument, verb and target triplets <Cite id="cholect50-benchmarking-2022" />.

In September 2026, Shutong Jin, Ken Goldberg and colleagues reported AGRO-SUVIDE, a coding-agent framework that builds debridement skills from one expert demonstration and retries a skill when its checks fail. In 340 physical trials on the da Vinci Research Kit, it removed single fragments from a viscoelastic substrate with 85% average success and completed three consecutive removals 60% of the time, or 95% with one human intervention <Cite id="agro-suvide-2026" />.

Intuitive says da Vinci 5's <Term id="force-feedback">Force Feedback</Term> measurements add a new data stream to surgical data science <Cite id="davinci5-clearance-2024" />, and Moon Surgical frames Maestro's sensing and onboard compute as the substrate for next-generation physical AI <Cite id="scopilot-clearance-2025" />. A 2022 review found surgical data science still lacking translational success stories, and its roadmap covers data acquisition under regulatory constraints, annotation and sharing <Cite id="maier-hein-sds-2022" />. The same question of how much evidence earns autonomy runs through [autonomous vehicles](/adjacent/autonomous-vehicles/), [drones](/adjacent/drones/) and [space robotics](/adjacent/space/).

Space robotics is the design and operation of robots beyond Earth, from planetary rovers to station arms and satellite servicers. A signal needs 4 to 20 minutes to reach Mars <Cite id="jpl-ipn-pnt-2024" />, so rovers drive mostly on their own <Cite id="enav-perseverance-2026" />, and commercial servicers have docked with satellites in orbit since 2020 <Cite id="mev1-servicing-2025" />.

<Image id="perseverance-selfie-rochette-2021" />

## Autonomy paced by the speed of light

NASA and JPL rovers have used onboard autonomy since 2004 <Cite id="mer-mobility-software-2006" />. Sheridan's 1993 review found that space teleoperation had tended to avoid time delay by not teleoperating from the ground <Cite id="sheridan-time-delay-1993" />. The Mars Exploration Rovers layered goal-based driving over reactive and predictive safety checks, and drove over 11,000 m combined by October 2005 <Cite id="mer-mobility-software-2006" />. They were the first robots to use visual odometry on another world, and within two years it grew from an "extra credit" capability into a critical vehicle safety system <Cite id="mer-visual-odometry-2007" />.

In Perseverance's first Mars year, AutoNav evaluated 88 percent of the 17.7 km driven, against Opportunity's previous record of 2.4 km over fourteen years <Cite id="perseverance-autonomy-2023" />. It drove 699.9 m without humans reviewing the imagery and 347.7 m in one sol, both planetary rover records <Cite id="perseverance-autonomy-2023" />. Its Enhanced Autonomous Navigation runs on a single-core CPU and raised average daily driving distance by an order of magnitude <Cite id="enav-perseverance-2026" />. By October 28, 2024, it had evaluated the terrain for about 90 percent of 32.1 km <Cite id="enav-perseverance-2026" />.

Since February 2026 Perseverance can [fix its own position](/classical/state-estimation/) by matching navcam panoramas to orbital imagery, to within 25 cm in about two minutes <Cite id="mars-global-localization-2026" />. In December 2025 JPL used [vision-language models](/manipulation/vla-models/) on the ground to generate Perseverance waypoints from HiRISE orbital imagery and terrain-slope data <Cite id="perseverance-ai-drive-2026" />. After a digital twin verified over 500,000 telemetry variables, the rover drove 210 m on December 8 and 246 m two days later <Cite id="perseverance-ai-drive-2026" />.

Onboard software also picks science targets. On Curiosity since 2016, AEGIS has increased science data return by selecting targets for the ChemCam laser spectrometer <Cite id="aegis-curiosity-2017" />. On Perseverance it picks SuperCam targets from wide-angle images during or right after long drives, without waiting for a ground cycle <Cite id="perseverance-autonomy-2023" />. In 2024 NASA described PIXL's "adaptive sampling" as the first use of AI on Mars to make autonomous decisions from real-time rock composition analysis <Cite id="pixl-adaptive-sampling-2024" />.

On April 19, 2021, Ingenuity made the first powered, controlled flight on another planet, in an atmosphere with about one percent of Earth's surface pressure <Cite id="ingenuity-first-flight-2021" />. Designed for five flights over thirty days, it flew 72 times in almost three years before NASA ended the mission in January 2024 <Cite id="ingenuity-mission-end-2024" />. NASA's accident investigation named the most likely cause: a lack of surface texture gave the navigation system too little information <Cite id="ingenuity-investigation-2024" />.

<Image id="ingenuity-mastcam-z-closeup-2021" />

## Living off the land: ISRU

MOXIE, on Perseverance, was the first demonstration of <Term id="in-situ-resource-utilization">in-situ resource utilization</Term> (ISRU) on another planet, making oxygen by solid-oxide electrolysis of atmospheric carbon dioxide <Cite id="moxie-sciadv-2022" />. A scaled-up version would make the tens of tons of oxygen an ascent rocket needs on Mars, instead of launching hundreds of tons from Earth <Cite id="moxie-sciadv-2022" />. Across sixteen runs MOXIE produced 122 grams of oxygen, peaking at 12 grams per hour at 98 percent purity or better, about twice NASA's original goals <Cite id="moxie-completion-2023" />. It concluded operations in September 2023 <Cite id="moxie-completion-2023" />.

<Image id="moxie-installation-perseverance-2020" />

Scaled ISRU means drilling and moving abrasive regolith in vacuum and cold. NASA's PRIME-1 suite reached the lunar south pole on Intuitive Machines' IM-2 lander in March 2025, where the lander, Athena, came to rest on its side in a crater <Cite id="prime-1-lunar-2025" />.

NASA put it about 400 m from its target and the mission at about ten hours of the ten days planned; the PRIME-1 team's 2026 paper gives about 500 m and 12 hours <Cite id="prime-1-lunar-2025" /><Cite id="hancock-prime1-2026" />. TRIDENT, Honeybee Robotics' one-metre rotary-percussive drill, executed its commanded motions, but with the lander on its side it could not reach the surface to excavate <Cite id="prime-1-lunar-2025" /><Cite id="hancock-prime1-2026" />. Initial data suggested the MSOLO mass spectrometer detected only gases of human origin, such as propellant and traces of Earth water <Cite id="prime-1-lunar-2025" />. In [evaluation](/data-hardware/evaluation-crisis/) terms PRIME-1 was one trial: the instruments worked while the landing cost the science <Cite id="prime-1-lunar-2025" />.

Firefly's Blue Ghost landed on March 2, 2025, four days before Athena, and all its NASA payloads operated <Cite id="blue-ghost-lister-2025" />. Its LISTER probe dug with gas to 1 m, the deepest robotic planetary subsurface thermal probe yet <Cite id="blue-ghost-lister-2025" />.

Learned locomotion meets the same regolith in analogue tests on the ground. In October 2026, Adrian Fuhrer, Marco Hutter and colleagues at ETH Zurich reported on a 2025 campaign in the ESA/DLR LUNA lunar analogue facility in Cologne, where the quadrupeds ANYmal-D and Magnecko walked loose regolith simulant and crater-like terrain. The robots could cross the simulant, but sinkage and slip, dust kicked up by foot contacts, and perception failures from overexposure, shadows and low-texture ground all degraded performance <Cite id="luna-legged-2026" />.

## Orbital robotics: servicing and removal

<Term id="on-orbit-servicing">On-orbit servicing</Term> covers satellite repair, refuelling, upgrades and debris removal <Cite id="space-manipulator-review-2025" />. It means matching a target's orbit, then docking with it or grasping it. An arm and its base satellite move each other, and in 1989 Umetani and Yoshida derived a generalized Jacobian from momentum conservation to control such arms <Cite id="umetani-yoshida-1989" />. A 2025 review organises capture control around free-floating and free-flying modes, from vision-based estimation to post-capture stabilisation <Cite id="space-manipulator-review-2025" />.

<OrbitalServicingTable className="my-6 wide-measure" />

ROTEX flew on Space Shuttle Columbia in early 1993, worked autonomously, under astronaut teleoperation and under ground control, and grasped free-floating objects <Cite id="rotex-1993" />. Japan's ETS-VII demonstrated autonomous rendezvous and docking between two satellites in 1998, with flight experiments for a 2 m, six-degree-of-freedom arm <Cite id="ets-vii-ard-2001" /><Cite id="ets-vii-robot-2001" />. In DARPA's 2007 Orbital Express, the ASTRO servicer autonomously captured NextSat and transferred propellant and a battery to it over four months <Cite id="orbital-express-2008" /><Cite id="boeing-orbital-express-2007" />.

On the International Space Station, Canadarm2, a 17 m arm, assembled the station and still grapples and berths arriving cargo vehicles <Cite id="canadarm2-csa-2024" />. Dextre, a two-armed robot that rides it, replaces exterior equipment including 100 kg batteries by <Term id="teleoperation">teleoperation</Term> from the ground <Cite id="dextre-csa-2024" />.

<Image id="dextre-canadarm2-iss-2017" />

In 2020 Northrop Grumman's MEV-1 made the first docking of two commercial spacecraft in orbit, capturing Intelsat 901 in the graveyard orbit above geosynchronous altitude and returning it to service <Cite id="mev1-servicing-2025" />. After five years it undocked, the first such undocking in that orbit, and moved to its next mission <Cite id="mev1-servicing-2025" />. On July 21, 2026, Northrop Grumman's Mission Robotic Vehicle launched with the DARPA-funded RSGS payload, twin robotic arms built by the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory <Cite id="rsgs-mrv-launch-2026" />. It will install small propulsion modules called mission extension pods to extend satellites' lives <Cite id="rsgs-mrv-launch-2026" />.

Debris is the uncooperative case, and ESA's 2026 report states that active debris removal is required to stop collisions multiplying debris <Cite id="esa-space-environment-2026" />. In 2024 Astroscale's ADRAS-J, flying for JAXA, inspected a discarded rocket upper stage in three fly-arounds and closed to about 15 m <Cite id="adras-j-15m-2024" />. No commercial spacecraft had come closer to debris, and the onboard collision-avoidance system aborted autonomously after an unexpected relative attitude anomaly <Cite id="adras-j-15m-2024" />.

By March 25, 2026, ADRAS-J had begun a controlled deorbit after 293 days in orbit <Cite id="adras-j-deorbit-2026" />. ADRAS-J2 targets launch in Japan's fiscal year 2027 to capture and remove an upper stage weighing about 3 t <Cite id="adras-j2-isar-2026" />.

NASA discontinued OSAM-1, a mission to refuel an unprepared satellite, in March 2024 after an independent review <Cite id="osam1-discontinued-2024" />. It cited technical, cost and schedule challenges and what it called a broader community evolution away from refuelling unprepared spacecraft, which left no committed partner <Cite id="osam1-discontinued-2024" />. In August 2026 NASA and Katalyst called off the LINK servicer's planned capture and boost of Swift, launched in 2004, over an attitude-control issue on the commercial spacecraft <Cite id="swift-boost-update-2026" />. NASA expected Swift to re-enter later in 2026 <Cite id="swift-boost-update-2026" />.

## What robot learning takes from it

Perception latency of tens of milliseconds caps a [drone's](/adjacent/drones/) safe speed <Cite id="falanga-latency-2019" />. Mars delays run to minutes, so spacecraft there must handle off-nominal situations without real-time commanding from Earth <Cite id="jpl-ipn-pnt-2024" />.

<SpaceLatencyLadder className="my-6" />

Learned control has flown on NASA's Astrobee free-flyers aboard the ISS. In 2025 Banerjee and colleagues reported the first in-space test of learned warm starts for trajectory optimization, while a convex solver still enforced safety <Cite id="banerjee-warm-starts-2025" />. The network cut solver iterations by 60 percent with rotational dynamics and 50 percent with in-distribution obstacles <Cite id="banerjee-warm-starts-2025" />. On May 27, 2025, the Naval Research Laboratory's APIARY team ran what it calls the first reinforcement-learning control of a free-flyer in space, with a policy trained in randomized simulation <Cite id="apiary-astrobee-2025" />.

The Space Robotics Bench authors say costly technology demonstrations and limited data severely hinder robot learning in space <Cite id="space-robotics-bench-2025" />. A September 2026 review adds space-specific dynamics and sensing, limited onboard resources and stringent safety requirements <Cite id="ai-space-robot-ops-review-2026" />. AI4MARS offers 326,000 crowdsourced terrain labels on 35,000 rover images, and a model trained on it exceeded 96 percent accuracy <Cite id="ai4mars-2021" />.

Space shares its [reliability](/frontier/reliability-gap/) bar with [surgical robotics](/adjacent/surgical/). Ingenuity flew more than fourteen times its five planned flights <Cite id="ingenuity-mission-end-2024" />, while OSAM-1 was cancelled before flight <Cite id="osam1-discontinued-2024" />. AEGIS and the digital-twin check on AI-planned drives both add autonomy in bounded, verified steps <Cite id="aegis-curiosity-2017" /><Cite id="perseverance-ai-drive-2026" />.

On Curiosity since 2016, AEGIS has increased science data return by selecting targets for the ChemCam laser spectrometer <Cite id="aegis-curiosity-2017" />. On Perseverance it picks SuperCam targets from wide-angle images during or right after long drives, without waiting for a ground cycle <Cite id="perseverance-autonomy-2023" />. In 2024 NASA described PIXL's "adaptive sampling" as the first use of AI on Mars to make autonomous decisions from real-time rock composition analysis <Cite id="pixl-adaptive-sampling-2024" />.

On April 19, 2021, Ingenuity made the first powered, controlled flight on another planet, in an atmosphere with about one percent of Earth's surface pressure <Cite id="ingenuity-first-flight-2021" />. Designed for five flights over thirty days, it flew 72 times in almost three years before NASA ended the mission in January 2024 <Cite id="ingenuity-mission-end-2024" />. NASA's accident investigation named the most likely cause: a lack of surface texture gave the navigation system too little information <Cite id="ingenuity-investigation-2024" />.

## Living off the land: ISRU

MOXIE, on Perseverance, was the first demonstration of <Term id="in-situ-resource-utilization">in-situ resource utilization</Term> (ISRU) on another planet, making oxygen by solid-oxide electrolysis of atmospheric carbon dioxide <Cite id="moxie-sciadv-2022" />. A scaled-up version would make the tens of tons of oxygen an ascent rocket needs on Mars, instead of launching hundreds of tons from Earth <Cite id="moxie-sciadv-2022" />. Across sixteen runs MOXIE produced 122 grams of oxygen, peaking at 12 grams per hour at 98 percent purity or better, about twice NASA's original goals <Cite id="moxie-completion-2023" />. It concluded operations in September 2023 <Cite id="moxie-completion-2023" />.

<Image id="moxie-installation-perseverance-2020" />

Scaled ISRU means drilling and moving abrasive regolith in vacuum and cold. NASA's PRIME-1 suite reached the lunar south pole on Intuitive Machines' IM-2 lander in March 2025, where the lander, Athena, came to rest on its side in a crater <Cite id="prime-1-lunar-2025" />.

NASA put it about 400 m from its target and the mission at about ten hours of the ten days planned; the PRIME-1 team's 2026 paper gives about 500 m and 12 hours <Cite id="prime-1-lunar-2025" /><Cite id="hancock-prime1-2026" />. TRIDENT, Honeybee Robotics' one-metre rotary-percussive drill, executed its commanded motions, but with the lander on its side it could not reach the surface to excavate <Cite id="prime-1-lunar-2025" /><Cite id="hancock-prime1-2026" />. Initial data suggested the MSOLO mass spectrometer detected only gases of human origin, such as propellant and traces of Earth water <Cite id="prime-1-lunar-2025" />. In [evaluation](/data-hardware/evaluation-crisis/) terms PRIME-1 was one trial: the instruments worked while the landing cost the science <Cite id="prime-1-lunar-2025" />.

Firefly's Blue Ghost landed on March 2, 2025, four days before Athena, and all its NASA payloads operated <Cite id="blue-ghost-lister-2025" />. Its LISTER probe dug with gas to 1 m, the deepest robotic planetary subsurface thermal probe yet <Cite id="blue-ghost-lister-2025" />.

Learned locomotion meets the same regolith in analogue tests on the ground. In October 2026, Adrian Fuhrer, Marco Hutter and colleagues at ETH Zurich reported on a 2025 campaign in the ESA/DLR LUNA lunar analogue facility in Cologne, where the quadrupeds ANYmal-D and Magnecko walked loose regolith simulant and crater-like terrain. The robots could cross the simulant, but sinkage and slip, dust kicked up by foot contacts, and perception failures from overexposure, shadows and low-texture ground all degraded performance <Cite id="luna-legged-2026" />.

Cave exploration adds route uncertainty. PLGRIM connects local risk-aware planning to global exploration goals and was tested on robots in Martian-analogue lava tubes <Cite id="plgrim-2021" />. Other work remains at the mission-concept stage: Olsen and Alexis propose jumping legged robots for lava tubes <Cite id="mars-jumping-2023" />, while ReachBot's MELT study proposes locomotion through extendable and retractable limbs <Cite id="reachbot-melt-2024" />.

## Orbital robotics: servicing and removal

<Term id="on-orbit-servicing">On-orbit servicing</Term> covers satellite repair, refuelling, upgrades and debris removal <Cite id="space-manipulator-review-2025" />. It means matching a target's orbit, then docking with it or grasping it. An arm and its base satellite move each other, and in 1989 Umetani and Yoshida derived a generalized Jacobian from momentum conservation to control such arms <Cite id="umetani-yoshida-1989" />. A 2025 review organises capture control around free-floating and free-flying modes, from vision-based estimation to post-capture stabilisation <Cite id="space-manipulator-review-2025" />.

Relative navigation needs labelled spacecraft images. SPEED combines synthetic and real imagery for monocular pose estimation <Cite id="speed-challenge-2019" />; SPEED+ adds hardware-in-the-loop images with controlled poses and space-like illumination <Cite id="speedplus-2021" />. SPARK instead supplies simulated RGB and depth images labelled by spacecraft or debris class <Cite id="spark-2021" />.

The renderer has to reproduce the sensing problem. URSO uses Unreal Engine 4 to generate labelled views of spacecraft orbiting Earth <Cite id="urso-2019" />. SurRender's CPU ray tracer uses double precision to handle the scale difference between celestial distances and local target detail <Cite id="surrender-2021" />.

<OrbitalServicingTable className="my-6 wide-measure" />

ROTEX flew on Space Shuttle Columbia in early 1993, worked autonomously, under astronaut teleoperation and under ground control, and grasped free-floating objects <Cite id="rotex-1993" />. Japan's ETS-VII demonstrated autonomous rendezvous and docking between two satellites in 1998, with flight experiments for a 2 m, six-degree-of-freedom arm <Cite id="ets-vii-ard-2001" /><Cite id="ets-vii-robot-2001" />. In DARPA's 2007 Orbital Express, the ASTRO servicer autonomously captured NextSat and transferred propellant and a battery to it over four months <Cite id="orbital-express-2008" /><Cite id="boeing-orbital-express-2007" />.

On the International Space Station, Canadarm2, a 17 m arm, assembled the station and still grapples and berths arriving cargo vehicles <Cite id="canadarm2-csa-2024" />. Dextre, a two-armed robot that rides it, replaces exterior equipment including 100 kg batteries by <Term id="teleoperation">teleoperation</Term> from the ground <Cite id="dextre-csa-2024" />.

<Image id="dextre-canadarm2-iss-2017" />

In 2020 Northrop Grumman's MEV-1 made the first docking of two commercial spacecraft in orbit, capturing Intelsat 901 in the graveyard orbit above geosynchronous altitude and returning it to service <Cite id="mev1-servicing-2025" />. After five years it undocked, the first such undocking in that orbit, and moved to its next mission <Cite id="mev1-servicing-2025" />. On July 21, 2026, Northrop Grumman's Mission Robotic Vehicle launched with the DARPA-funded RSGS payload, twin robotic arms built by the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory <Cite id="rsgs-mrv-launch-2026" />. It will install small propulsion modules called mission extension pods to extend satellites' lives <Cite id="rsgs-mrv-launch-2026" />.

Debris is the uncooperative case, and ESA's 2026 report states that active debris removal is required to stop collisions multiplying debris <Cite id="esa-space-environment-2026" />. In 2024 Astroscale's ADRAS-J, flying for JAXA, inspected a discarded rocket upper stage in three fly-arounds and closed to about 15 m <Cite id="adras-j-15m-2024" />. No commercial spacecraft had come closer to debris, and the onboard collision-avoidance system aborted autonomously after an unexpected relative attitude anomaly <Cite id="adras-j-15m-2024" />.

By March 25, 2026, ADRAS-J had begun a controlled deorbit after 293 days in orbit <Cite id="adras-j-deorbit-2026" />. ADRAS-J2 targets launch in Japan's fiscal year 2027 to capture and remove an upper stage weighing about 3 t <Cite id="adras-j2-isar-2026" />.

NASA discontinued OSAM-1, a mission to refuel an unprepared satellite, in March 2024 after an independent review <Cite id="osam1-discontinued-2024" />. It cited technical, cost and schedule challenges and what it called a broader community evolution away from refuelling unprepared spacecraft, which left no committed partner <Cite id="osam1-discontinued-2024" />. In August 2026 NASA and Katalyst called off the LINK servicer's planned capture and boost of Swift, launched in 2004, over an attitude-control issue on the commercial spacecraft <Cite id="swift-boost-update-2026" />. NASA expected Swift to re-enter later in 2026 <Cite id="swift-boost-update-2026" />.

## What robot learning takes from it

Perception latency of tens of milliseconds caps a [drone's](/adjacent/drones/) safe speed <Cite id="falanga-latency-2019" />. Mars delays run to minutes, so spacecraft there must handle off-nominal situations without real-time commanding from Earth <Cite id="jpl-ipn-pnt-2024" />.

<SpaceLatencyLadder className="my-6" />

Learned control has flown on NASA's Astrobee free-flyers aboard the ISS. In 2025 Banerjee and colleagues reported the first in-space test of learned warm starts for trajectory optimization, while a convex solver still enforced safety <Cite id="banerjee-warm-starts-2025" />. The network cut solver iterations by 60 percent with rotational dynamics and 50 percent with in-distribution obstacles <Cite id="banerjee-warm-starts-2025" />. On May 27, 2025, the Naval Research Laboratory's APIARY team ran what it calls the first reinforcement-learning control of a free-flyer in space, with a policy trained in randomized simulation <Cite id="apiary-astrobee-2025" />.

The Space Robotics Bench authors say costly technology demonstrations and limited data severely hinder robot learning in space <Cite id="space-robotics-bench-2025" />. A September 2026 review adds space-specific dynamics and sensing, limited onboard resources and stringent safety requirements <Cite id="ai-space-robot-ops-review-2026" />. AI4MARS offers 326,000 crowdsourced terrain labels on 35,000 rover images, and a model trained on it exceeded 96 percent accuracy <Cite id="ai4mars-2021" />.

Space shares its [reliability](/frontier/reliability-gap/) bar with [surgical robotics](/adjacent/surgical/). Ingenuity flew more than fourteen times its five planned flights <Cite id="ingenuity-mission-end-2024" />, while OSAM-1 was cancelled before flight <Cite id="osam1-discontinued-2024" />. AEGIS and the digital-twin check on AI-planned drives both add autonomy in bounded, verified steps <Cite id="aegis-curiosity-2017" /><Cite id="perseverance-ai-drive-2026" />.
